query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: theme_crew_service
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary present/absent flag for a review theme (6930 vs 1170). This is exactly the kind of external, associational variable the query wants: reviews can be segmented by whether they mention crew service and their mean Overall Rating compared.

per_column.name: theme_seat_comfort
per_column.rationale: Binary theme flag with well-balanced groups (4551 vs 3549). Cleanly groupable and directly comparable against the focus, supporting the higher/lower rating comparison.

per_column.name: theme_food_quality
per_column.rationale: Binary theme indicator with well-separated categories (4986 vs 3114). Meaningful segmentation axis for relating a theme to Overall Rating.

per_column.name: theme_entertainment
per_column.rationale: Binary theme flag (3232 present / 4868 absent). Interpretable and groupable; supports comparing rating for reviews that raise entertainment vs. those that don't.

per_column.name: theme_punctuality
per_column.rationale: Binary punctuality theme flag with balanced groups (3620 vs 4480). Clear associational segmentation variable for the focus.

per_column.name: theme_value_money
per_column.rationale: Binary theme flag (2513 vs 5587). Both groups are large enough for a meaningful rating comparison, satisfying the EDA claim.

per_column.name: theme_cleanliness
per_column.rationale: Binary theme indicator (1449 vs 6651). Somewhat imbalanced but both cells are still populous enough to segment on and compare against Overall Rating.

per_column.name: theme_boarding
per_column.rationale: Binary boarding theme flag (6290 vs 1810). Interpretable, groupable, and directly relevant to the 'which themes' question.

per_column.name: review_sentiment_score
per_column.rationale: A bare, fine-grained sentiment polarity score. It is largely a proxy/near-restatement of Overall Rating (both measure review positivity), and its many idiosyncratic fractional values (0.3333, 0.7143, ...) are an opaque scale rather than clean interpretable categories. Weak for human-facing segmentation.

per_column.name: review_word_count
per_column.rationale: A generic, mechanical text-length feature. As given it is spread across dozens of near-uniform integer values with no natural, interpretable breakpoints, so no meaningful comparison against the focus can be drawn without ad-hoc binning. Explicitly the kind of token/length count that does not realise the EDA claim.

per_column.name: traveller_class_segment
per_column.rationale: Concatenation of Type of Traveller and Class into well-separated, human-readable categories. It is redundant with two existing columns rather than an external variable, but it directly provides the cross-segmentation axis the query calls for ('Across Type of Traveller and Class') and is highly interpretable to group on.

per_column.name: segment_mean_rating
per_column.rationale: This is an aggregate of the focus itself (mean Overall Rating per segment). It restates/leaks the focus variable rather than supplying an independent associational variable, so it cannot open a genuine relationship for discovery.

per_column.name: rating_vs_segment_mean
per_column.rationale: A direct arithmetic transformation of the focus (Overall Rating minus its segment mean). It is derived from and restates the focus, and its values are fine-grained deviations, offering no external variable to compare against.

judge.rationale: The eight binary theme flags are an excellent realisation of the exploratory intent: they are interpretable, well-separated present/absent segments that let a human compare mean Overall Rating across each theme, exactly answering 'which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower rating.' The traveller_class_segment adds the requested Type-of-Traveller x Class grouping axis (though redundant with existing columns). However, the set is diluted by weak/invalid additions: review_word_count is a mechanical length feature with no interpretable breaks, review_sentiment_score is a fine-grained bare-sentiment near-restatement of the focus, and both segment_mean_rating and rating_vs_segment_mean are aggregates/transforms of Overall Rating itself (focus leakage, not associational variables). The strong theme core keeps informativeness fairly high, but the focus-derived restatements and mechanical columns prevent a top score.
